extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents) and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules for supplemental examination / ex parte reexamination procedures and for determining eligibility, calculation, reduction, and caps on patent term adjustments due to USPTO examination delay under URAA and the Patent Term Guarantee Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination: substantial new question determination
rubrics_metrics.description: “the determination whether any of the items of information presented in the request raised a substantial new question of patentability.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the supplemental examination certificate states that a substantial new question of patentability is raised by one or more items, ex parte reexamination will be ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257. If the certificate indicates no substantial new question is raised and ex parte reexamination is not ordered, the supplemental examination certificate will be published and the reexamination fee will be refunded in accordance with § 1.26(c). The electronically issued supplemental examination certificate remains part of the public record of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257: procedural modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: When ex parte reexamination is ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 as a result of supplemental examination, the reexamination will be conducted under §§ 1.530–1.570 except as modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications include: (1) The patent owner will not have the right to file a statement pursuant to § 1.530 and the order will not set a time period to file such a statement; (2) Reexamination of any claim may be conducted on the basis of any item of information as set forth in § 1.605 and is not limited to patents and printed publications or to subject matter added/deleted during the reexamination, notwithstanding § 1.552(a); (3) Issues in addition to those raised by patents and printed publications and by subject matter added/deleted may be considered and resolved, notwithstanding § 1.552(c); and (4) Information material to patentability will be defined by § 1.56(b), notwithstanding § 1.555(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension eligibility under URAA (§ 1.701)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent (other than design) issued on an application filed on or after June 8, 1995 and before May 29, 2000 is entitled to extension of the patent term if issuance was delayed due to: (1) interference or derivation proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 135(a); and/or (2) the application being placed under a secrecy order under 35 U.S.C. 181; and/or (3) appellate review by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board or by a Federal court under 35 U.S.C. 141 or 145 where the patent was issued pursuant to a decision reversing an adverse determination of patentability (with remand specifics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A remand by a PTAB panel is considered a decision reversing an adverse determination only if the remand is the last action by a panel prior to mailing of a notice of allowance and provided certain subsequent RCE/office action conditions are not met (see detailed remand rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount and running of URAA extension (§ 1.701(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent entitled to extension under paragraph (a) shall be extended for the sum of the periods of delay calculated under paragraphs (c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(3) and (d) of this section, to the extent that these periods are not overlapping, up to a maximum of five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extension will run from the expiration date of the patent. Overlap of delay periods is not double-counted when computing the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference/derivation delay calculation (URAA § 1.701(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each interference or derivation proceeding in which the application was involved, count the number of days beginning on the date the proceeding was instituted to involve the application and ending on the date the proceeding was terminated with respect to the application; plus any days the application prosecution was suspended by the Office due to other interference/derivation proceedings not involving the application (institution-to-termination and suspension intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays are counted only to the extent they are not overlapping with other delay periods considered for adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment grounds under the Patent Term Guarantee Act — failure to take actions (§ 1.702(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An original patent (other than design) may be adjusted if issuance was delayed due to the failure of the Office to take specified actions within set timeframes, specifically: (1) mail at least one notification under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 not later than 14 months after filing or national stage commencement; (2) respond to a reply under 35 U.S.C. 132 or to an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 134 not later than 4 months after filing/taking; (3) act on an application not later than 4 months after a PTAB or Federal court decision where at least one allowable claim remains; or (4) issue a patent not later than 4 months after issue fee payment and all requirements satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grounds are subject to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and the subpart. (Editor notes indicate applicability to patents granted on or after certain dates.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year pendency ground (§ 1.702(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed due to the Office failing to issue a patent within three years after filing or national stage commencement (subject to 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and this subpart), but not including specified excluded time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded periods include time consumed by continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b), interference/derivation proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 135(a), imposition of a secrecy order under 35 U.S.C. 181, review by PTAB or Federal court, and any delay in processing requested by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays caused by interference and derivation proceedings (§ 1.702(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed due to interference or derivation proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 135(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculation of the period(s) of delay follows rules in § 1.703(c) to avoid double-counting overlapping periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays caused by secrecy order (§ 1.702(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed due to the application being placed under a secrecy order under 35 U.S.C. 181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculation of the period(s) of delay follows rules in § 1.703(d); included are time in sealed condition and periods related to examiner's answers and notifications tied to the secrecy order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays caused by successful appellate review (§ 1.702(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed due to review by the PTAB or by a Federal court under specified statutes, if the patent was issued pursuant to a decision in the review reversing an adverse determination of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remand-by-panel rules apply: a remand is treated as a decision reversing an adverse determination (and as a final decision in favor of the applicant under § 1.703(e)) only if the remand is the last panel action prior to mailing of a notice of allowance and if it is not followed by an RCE that was not first preceded by a mailing after such remand of an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment calculation for § 1.702(a) (§ 1.703(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under § 1.702(a) is the sum of the following non-overlapping periods (1) days from the day after 14 months after filing/national stage to mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 (whichever first); (2) days from day after 4 months after filing a reply under § 1.111 to mailing of action/notice of allowance; (3) days from day after 4 months after filing a reply in compliance with § 1.113(c) to mailing of action/notice of allowance; (4) days from day after 4 months after filing an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 to mailing of any examiner's answer under § 41.39, action under 35 U.S.C. 132, or notice of allowance; (5) days from day after 4 months after final PTAB or Federal court decision where at least one allowable claim remains to mailing of action/notice of allowance; and (6) days from day after 4 months after issue fee paid & requirements satisfied to patent issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed interval is counted only to the extent it is non-overlapping with other counted periods; the definition uses 'day after' and specific triggering mailings/actions to determine interval endpoints. Editor notes specify applicability dates for some subparagraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period calculation for three-year pendency (§ 1.703(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under § 1.702(b) is the number of days in the period beginning the day after three years from filing/national stage commencement and ending on the date a patent was issued, but not including specified excluded periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded periods (which are subtracted from the three-year interval) include RCE time (35 U.S.C. 132(b)), interference/derivation institution-to-termination and related suspensions, time maintained in sealed condition under secrecy order and related secrecy-order intervals, and periods when jurisdiction passes to and ends with the PTAB (see § 1.703(b)(1)-(4) for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap rule, cap, and running of adjustment (§ 1.703(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent that periods of delay attributable to grounds in § 1.702 overlap, the period of adjustment granted shall not exceed the actual number of days the issuance was delayed. The term shall be adjusted for the sum of the non-overlapping periods under §§ 1.703(a)–(e), less the sum of periods calculated under § 1.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The adjustment will run from the patent expiration date set forth in 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2). The date on a certificate of mailing or transmission under § 1.8 is not taken into account in the calculation. No patent disclaimed beyond a specified date shall be adjusted beyond the disclaimer expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for failure to engage in reasonable efforts (§ 1.704(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment shall be reduced by a period equal to the period during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction applies with respect to the grounds for adjustment set forth in §§ 1.702(a)–(e) and impacts the cumulative adjustment amount (see § 1.703(f) which subtracts reductions under § 1.704).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month cumulative reply delay reduction (§ 1.704(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is deemed to have failed to engage in reasonable efforts for the cumulative total of any periods of time in excess of three months taken to reply to any Office notice/action that requires a rejection, objection, argument, or other request, measuring the three-month period from the date the Office communication was mailed or given to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cumulative reply delays exceed the three-month threshold, the period of adjustment is reduced by the number of days beginning the day after the three-month point and ending on the date the reply was filed. The Office action's set or shortened statutory reply period does not affect the three-month measurement in § 1.704(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances constituting failure to engage (specific reductions) (§ 1.704(c)(1)-(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific applicant actions or events that constitute failure to engage (each resulting in a reduction of the adjustment for the number of days specified) include: (1) suspension of action under § 1.103 at applicant’s request (reduction from request date to termination of suspension); (2) deferral of issuance under § 1.314 (reduction from deferral request to termination or earlier issuance); (3) abandonment of the application or late payment of issue fee (reduction from abandonment or day after fee due to date revival petition/late payment petition filed); (4) failure to file petition to withdraw abandonment or revive within two months from mailing of abandonment notice (reduction from day after two-month deadline to petition filing date); (5) conversion of a provisional to nonprovisional under 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5) (reduction from provisional filing to compliant conversion request under § 1.53(c)(3)); (6) submission of a preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper less than one month before mailing of an Office action or notice of allowance that requires a supplemental action (reduction from eight months after filing/commencement date to date preliminary paper filed); (7) submission of a reply having an omission (§ 1.135(c)) (reduction from day after filing omitted-reply to date correction filed); (8) submission of a supplemental reply/paper after a reply has been filed (unless expressly requested by examiner) (reduction from day after initial reply to date supplemental reply filed); (9) submission of an amendment/paper after a PTAB or Federal court decision (except certain new-ground decisions) less than one month before mailing of an Office action or notice of allowance that requires a supplemental action (reduction from day after decision to date amendment/paper filed); (10) submission of an amendment under § 1.312 or other paper (unless expressly requested by Office or an RCE request in compliance with § 1.114) after a notice of allowance, (reduction from day after notice of allowance to date amendment/paper filed); and (11) failure to file an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 within three ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed circumstance specifies the exact interval for which the adjustment is reduced (beginning and ending dates are defined per subparagraph). The rule text provides precise measurement rules tailored to each circumstance; note that (11) continues beyond the chunked text and refers to failure to file an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 within three months (with associated reduction consequences). Reductions are only applied to the extent such periods are not overlapping with other reductions.
